title: Contextual Fusebook and Safe Fallback Blueprint
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a contextual "fusebook" (a lightweight per-entity circuit and fallback registry) to provide safe, observable, and SLO-aligned trip behaviour across dependencies (storage/cache), models, and tenants. The goal is deterministic, auditable degraded paths and automated fallbacks that preserve availability while protecting tail latencies and cost targets.
background: We run into cascading outages or high-cost spikes when a dependent model or external service oscillates. Current heuristics (global thresholds) are either too aggressive for small tenants or too lax for bursty customers. We need a flexible, runtime-configurable system that computes trippoints using multiple signals (error rate, latency quantiles, queue depth, cost-per-token) and routes to safe fallback variants (cached responses, lower-cost quantized models, regional replicas) without manual intervention.
goals: Per-entity circuits: support dependency/model/tenant-level circuits with inheritance and overrides
SLO-aligned trip logic: compute trip thresholds relative to target SLOs (p95/p99 latency, error rate budgets)
Safe fallback catalog: automated safe fallbacks including cached prefix, stateless heuristic reply, downgraded model family, and region failover
Observability and auditable decisioning for every trip and fallback action
Graceful re-entry: controlled ramping to avoid flapping (hysteresis + canary traffic)
non_goals: Replacing global autoscaling policies (this complements autoscaling)
Full per-customer SLA contracts — we aim for operational defaults and tooling to escalate to SRE/CS
acceptance_criteria: Configurable circuit entries for dependency, model, and tenant levels
Trips computed from a weighted multi-signal function (latency quantiles, error rate, queue length, cost) and param-driven per-entity modifiers
Fallbacks executed automatically with route chosen according to a safe-fallback policy and recorded in tracing/logs
Simulated failure tests (chaos) show 90% reduction in downstream error blast radius with <5% added overall latency for healthy traffic
Dashboards show per-entity trip rate, fallback rate, and SLO spend; alerts fire when fallback rate exceeds threshold
design_decisions: Use a layered evaluation: tenant overrides > model overrides > dependency defaults
Trip score = sum(signal_i * weight_i) with exponential smoothing. Signals: p95_latency_normalized, p99_latency_normalized, error_rate, queue_depth_norm, cost_per_request_norm
Two-tier trip states: SOFT_TRIP (probabilistic shedding with sample fraction) and HARD_TRIP (full reroute to fallback). Soft trips allow partial traffic to continue while gathering recovery signals

Fallback priority list per entity: 1) cached prefix reply, 2) reduced-compute quantized model in same region, 3) regional replica (failover), 4) stateless heuristic reply (e.g., canned apology + backoff), 5) reject with graceful 429 + Retry-After
Hysteresis policy: min_open_seconds, backoff_factor, canary_recovery_window (percent traffic to re-open)
Persist trip events and decisions to the control plane for auditing and postmortems
implementation_steps: Schema: extend runtime config with 'fusebook' entries (entity_type, entity_id, weights, thresholds, fallback_chain, hysteresis) stored in config-store
Scoring engine: implement lightweight scoring service in runtime path (C++/Rust), with bounded CPU and async enrichment from metrics service
Routing integration: add fallback router that can route to cached layer, model variant, or remote region; ensure KV cache and prefix cache are accessible from router
Soft-trip path: probabilistic sampler module that marks requests for degraded treatment and records tracing tags
Observability: add metrics (trip_score, trip_state, fallback_kind, fallback_latency, fallback_success_rate) and traces for decision path; build dashboard templates
Chaos & e2e tests: synthetic load generator to trigger trips across tenancy sizes and validate safe fallback metrics
Docs & SDKs: API to query and update fusebook entries; CLI and console UI for SRE/PM to edit and view entries
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary runtime): Implement scoring + local fallback to cached prefix only. Rollout to 5% of infra with low-impact tenants
Phase 2 (Model-level rollouts): Enable quantized model fallback for 10% of calls; run internal traffic tests; validate cost and latency impact
Phase 3 (Tenant opt-in): Expose fusebook UI in console for a set of pilot customers; gather feedback
Phase 4 (Global): Enable full fallback chain and multi-region failover with automatic routing for eligible tenants; default conservative weights
Rollback: immediate global kill-switch in console and ability to pin per-tenant fusebook entry to OFF
telemetry_and_alerting: Per-entity p95/p99 latency and error-rate time series tagged with trip_state
Alert when fallback_rate > 1% for > 10min for customer-impact=high tenants
Alert when trip_score variance > configured threshold (indicates noisy signal or miscalibration)
Daily report of top 10 tripped entities and fallback actions for SRE review
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring, hysteresis, and probabilistic sampler
Integration tests that simulate model degradation and assert fallback path correctness and metrics
Chaos: inject regional latency spikes, increased error rates, and simulated model OOMs; measure blast radius reduction
Performance: ensure scoring adds <0.5ms median overhead on critical path and bounded 99th percentile impact
Security: ensure fusebook config updates authorized via RBAC and audited
notes: Decision: start with additive scoring to keep initial calibration simple; revisit ML-based classifier in Q3 if calibration drifts
We should coordinate with Dedicated team to ensure private deployments can opt for stricter defaults (shorter hysteresis)
Follow-up ticket: UI for visualizing per-tenant fallback traces and timeline
